title: More than 100,000 People in Japan Are 100 or Older
paragraphs: Japan now has more than 100,000 people who are 100 years old or older. It is the first time that the number has passed 100,000.

According to Japan's health ministry, there were 107,677 people aged 100 or older in Japan as of September 1, 2026. This was 7,914 more than a year before. The number has gone up every year for 56 years in a row.
Most of these people are women. There were 94,298 women aged 100 or older, which is about 88% of the total. There were 13,379 men.
The ministry released the numbers just before Respect for the Aged Day, a national holiday in Japan. It also expects 54,294 more people to turn 100 during the 2026 fiscal year.

The oldest woman in Japan is Fuyo Kishimoto, who is 114 years old and lives in Kyoto. She is the last living Japanese person who was born in the Meiji period, which ended in 1912. The oldest man is Hikaru Kato, who is 112 and lives in Kumamoto.
The number of people aged 100 or older has grown very quickly. In 1963, when Japan started counting them, there were only 153. The number passed 1,000 in 1981 and 10,000 in 1998.

Some parts of Japan have more people aged 100 or older than others. Shimane Prefecture had the most for its population, with about 187 for every 100,000 people. It was followed by Kochi, Tottori, Kagoshima and Nagano. Saitama Prefecture had the fewest, with about 51.
In general, there are more people aged 100 or older in western Japan than in eastern Japan.
